outcome: mode of delivery (emergency caesarean section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: 120 patients admitted to the labor room of VIMSAR, Burla, with complaints of bleeding per vaginal after 28 weeks of gestation and before delivery.
finding: Antepartum hemorrhage (APH) is a high-risk pregnancy associated with maternal and perinatal morbidities and mortality, requiring emergency care.
mod_finding: 71.7% of APH cases underwent emergency caesarean section and 28.3% underwent vaginal delivery, with specific rates varying by APH type (e.g., 100% of placenta previa cases had C-section).
